name: Butter knife
description: A blunt table knife with a rounded tip, for spreading.
notes: A stainless table knife 210 mm long lying flat, held by its handle. CHECK VOLUME (x0.25): the reference's 75 mL is a carried volume, not the steel. The plastic knife rides here as the brief has variants do; the vegetable peeler has a different head and would suit its own model if it gains a peeling use.

name: Cast-iron skillet
description: A heavy cast-iron frying pan with a long handle and a lug on the far side.
notes: A skillet 270 mm across with a 140 mm handle and a helper lug, iron-cast with a coal-black hanging hole. The reference's hammering quality is kept for its weight; a melee profile is left for weapon tuning. The steel, copper and aluminium pans have their own drafts sharing this model.

name: Steel frying pan
description: A light stainless frying pan with a long handle.
notes: Shares the pan model, recoloured. The reference weighs it at 660 g, which the shared model's mass does not follow; set its mass when the drafts are applied. Too light to bring hammering.

name: Copper frying pan
description: A copper frying pan with a long handle.
notes: Shares the pan model, recoloured. The reference weighs it at 628 g, which the shared model's mass does not follow; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Aluminium frying pan
description: A thin aluminium frying pan with a long handle.
notes: Shares the pan model, recoloured. The reference weighs it at 400 g, which the shared model's mass does not follow; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Pizza cutter
description: A steel cutting wheel on a plastic handle.
notes: A wheel 100 mm across on a fork and a plastic-red handle, 230 mm long, lying flat. The reference gives it no qualities; a rolling wheel makes a poor cutting tool, so it brings none.

name: Child's bowl
description: A small bright plastic bowl made for a child.
notes: A bowl 120 mm across and 48 mm tall, plastic-orange with a plastic-white non-slip ring. CHECK VOLUME (x5.3): the reference's 131 mL is the plastic, while the box counts the open bowl.

name: Plastic plate
description: A tough plastic dinner plate.
notes: A plate 256 mm across with a sloping rim, plastic-blue. CHECK VOLUME (x6): the box counts the air over a flat plate; stacked plates take little room.

name: Drinking straw
description: A bendable plastic drinking straw.
notes: A red straw 6 mm across and 200 mm long with a ribbed elbow and its short end bent up. Mass is the reference's 19.6 g, far above a real straw's half gram; set it lower when the drafts are applied if that matters. CHECK VOLUME (x5): the box counts the bend.

name: Cooking pot
description: A steel stock pot with two handles and a lid.
notes: A pot 190 mm across and 130 mm deep with riveted loop handles and a domed lid with a plastic-black knob, steel-stainless. The aluminium pot has its own draft on this model.

name: Aluminium pot
description: A light aluminium pot with two handles and a lid.
notes: Shares the pot model, recoloured. The reference weighs it at 231 g and 2.1 L, which the shared model does not follow; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Canning pot
description: A 20 litre enamelled pot with a lid and a wire rack for jars.
notes: A canner 360 mm across and 260 mm tall, paint-drum-blue for dark enamel (no speckled enamel finish exists), with plastic-black handles and knob and steel-galvanised rack handles resting on the rim. Its size is a placeholder for a thing too big to carry far. The pressure cooker and clay pot oven ride here as the brief has variants do, though a locking lid and a heavy clay pot would each read better on their own model. The clay canning pot has its own draft on this model.

name: Clay canning pot
description: A large fired-clay pot with a lid, big enough to boil jars in.
notes: Shares the pot_canning model, recoloured clay-terracotta. A crafted pot would lack the wire rack and moulded handles; the reference weighs it at 8.4 kg, which the shared model's mass does not follow; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Copper pot
description: A tin-lined copper pot with brass handles and a lid.
notes: A pot 180 mm across and 140 mm deep: copper shell, steel-grey tin lining inside, brass handles and lid knob.

name: Hammered steel pot
description: A rough pot beaten out of a sheet of steel.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. A lopsided shell 200 mm across its crimped rim with hammer marks and a wire bail. Mass is the reference's 6 kg, drawn with 8 mm walls; that weight reads as the steel sheet it was made from rather than a real pot, so lower it when the drafts are applied if that matters. CHECK VOLUME (x6): the reference's 1 L is its capacity, the box counts the bail.

name: Hammered copper pot
description: A rough pot beaten out of copper sheet.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. The hammered pot drawn in copper with verdigris hammer marks and thinner walls; it is its own row rather than a recolour because its walls differ. CHECK VOLUME (x5.9): the box counts the bail.

name: Rolling pin
description: A turned hardwood rolling pin with a handle at each end. Heavy enough to swing.
notes: A wood-birch pin 460 mm long with a 300 mm barrel 64 mm across, held by one handle. It would make a blunt club; a melee profile is left for weapon tuning.

name: Sippy cup
description: A child's plastic cup with two grips and a spill-proof spouted lid.
notes: A cup 70 mm across and 112 mm tall to the spout, plastic-blue with a plastic-white lid, spout to the front. CHECK VOLUME (x6.5): the reference's 131 mL is the plastic, the box counts the cup and grips.

name: Splatter screen
description: A round of fine steel mesh on a long handle, laid over a pan to stop spitting fat.
notes: A screen 290 mm across, 450 mm long with its handle, lying flat: a grid of steel-stainless wires at 12 mm pitch standing for the fine mesh, which no steel mesh finish shows, in a rolled rim with a plastic-black grip. sieving is a new quality name for the reference's sieve and strain qualities. CHECK VOLUME (x5.9): the reference's 500 mL counts it flat; the box adds the handle's sweep.

name: Spoon
description: A stainless dessert spoon.
notes: A spoon 190 mm long lying on its back, steel-stainless with a steel-mirror well. The plastic spoons ride here as the brief has variants do. The ladle, whisk, garlic press, spatula, ice cream scoop and grater are distinct utensils that the reference copies from the spoon; each would read better on its own model if it gains a use of its own.
